comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks an industrial shock absorber through iterative impact-response tuning; PR-1937 selectively closes only initially open push-latch cabinet doors.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key insertion, setscrew loosening/tightening, bimanual counterholding, fine collar rotation, bounded torque, and repeated physical cycling. PR-1937 requires identifying ajar doors and pressing their hinged panels until latching. Physical button/door pressing is only a generic shared primitive, not the tested ability.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe, repeatable dynamic stops within a 12.0 mm stroke and published energy/velocity limits, with no hard-stop strike, excessive rebound, overload, or lock drift. PR-1937 requires all initially open doors latched for 1 s and zero disturbance of initially closed doors. Candidate leaves rebound, overload, drift-tolerance, and tightening-torque thresholds undeclared; PR-1937 gives no force/travel threshold and emulates its latch each physics step, but these omissions do not create plausible duplication.
comparison.reason: The tasks test meaningfully different abilities: mechanical commissioning and retention of a dynamically tuned damper versus state-selective closure of toggle-latched doors. Their objectives, central manipulation sequences, failure modes, and completion tests do not overlap beyond generic contact actuation.
